info.title: WatchLog API
info.description: The public WatchLog API: what an API token can read, for Kubernetes clusters and Docker fleets. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (Settings → API tokens). Stability (ADR-126): additions may come in any release. A breaking change comes only with /api/v2, or after a deprecation that lasts two minor versions. Routes not listed here are the dashboard's own and may change without notice.

get.summary: Search a cluster by name
get.description: The ⌘K palette's search (ADR-169): workloads, pods and nodes of a Kubernetes cluster; hosts, containers and Compose projects of a Docker fleet; applications, certificates and scheduled jobs on both. Case-insensitive; a word matches when its letters appear in order in the name (with its namespace, Compose project or type), or with one letter off for words of 4 to 32 letters. The exact name first, then names starting with the query, then names containing it, then the rest. At most 8 per kind.

get.summary: Suggested egress policy for a workload
get.description: A suggested egress policy for one Kubernetes workload (ADR-190), built from what it was seen using: in-cluster destinations from the flow series (30 days, or the metrics retention if shorter), external names and networks from the egress inventory (last seen in 30 days), the expectations that cover it, and DNS to kube-dns. Two flavours: a standard NetworkPolicy (addresses only: a name becomes any public address on its port) and a CiliumNetworkPolicy with toFQDNs; the detected one first (ADR-191). YAML text only: WatchLog never applies it. A Docker fleet answers 404: Docker has no egress policy object.

get.description: What left its usual range in a cluster or a fleet (ADR-199): around an alert (60 minutes before it started to 15 minutes after, or now), or in a range of at most 24 hours (the last hour by default). At most 50 rows by start (`first`) or by how far out they went (`furthest`), with `total` and `truncated`; the unusual-activity chart; the learning state (nothing is listed for 7 days from the upgrade; `learning` says which day it is, when it is ready and which hours of the week have a baseline); and the probable cause's short form. Pro: 403 `pro-feature` for Cloud orgs without it; a self-hosted Community install answers 404.

id.description: A monitored service's id, for its page

peer.description: A map edge's destination; null for every other key

usualLow.description: The usual range at the start’s hour of the week

value.description: The latest value while it lasts, the furthest once ended

peakScore.description: How far out it went: distance from usual in spreads

own.description: One of WatchLog's own parts (its charts' workloads, its containers, its agent's units); listed only with `own=show`

more.description: Other changes of the same series in the window: the list shows a series once, its strongest current change (ADR-229)

rows.description: The episode's series, once each, by first move

anyOf.description: The selected episode told (ADR-231); null when the window has none

changes.description: What changed in the chart's range: its markers (rollouts, scaling, image changes, service starts and restarts, scheduled runs)
